# PhysicsHold

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/PhysicsHold.cs#L298)

One hand holding one object, without ever teleporting it. The object stays a full rigidbody the
whole time, so it collides with the world, sweeps what it touches, and already has the right motion
when it is let go.

The object's velocity is written each step so that integrating it lands the object on the
pose the grip asks for. Nothing iterates and nothing converges: the pose is arithmetic, and
the only things that can move the object off it are contacts, which is what should move it.

Holds on one object know about each other, which is what keeps exactly one of them driving it:
two writers on one body is a tug of war with no solver to arbitrate it.

```csharp
public sealed class PhysicsHold
```

### GripInBody {#gripinbody}

Where this hand's grip sits in the object's own space.

From the offset recorded at the grab, except for a hand working a part, where it is read
off the part every step. A part travels through the object it sits on, so a hand holding
one is somewhere different in that object's frame after every stroke, and an offset frozen
at the grab describes where the foregrip used to be.

### IsShortHanded {#isshorthanded}

Whether the object is being held by fewer hands than it wants. Either the object says so - a
crate marked as needing two - or the place being held does: a hand on a rifle's foregrip with
nothing on the grip is holding the end of a lever. A hand on the grip alone is not
short-handed unless the rifle says it is.

### PositionInGrip {#positioningrip}

Where the hand's grip sits in the object's own space right now, in metres. It should stay at
[`GripInBody`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHold#gripinbody); the difference is the hand slipping on what it holds. Measured in
the object's frame rather than the grip's, so a hand declining to roll with a rod does not
read as sliding along it.

### TurnsTheHand {#turnsthehand}

Whether turning this object turns the hand with it. The one thing it changes is where the hand
takes its own rotation from; the object is held exactly as firmly either way, so it does
nothing unless something else is turning the object - which in practice means a constraint.

### SettleWhenReleased(Rigidbody, bool, bool) {#settlewhenreleased-rigidbody-boolean-boolean}

Tells every hand holding an object what its rigidbody should be when they let go.

A hold remembers what the object was when it took it and puts that back on release, which
is right until something else changes what the object is underneath it. A socket handing a
cell back to the player mid-pull is exactly that: the hold took a kinematic body out of a
socket, and left alone it would hand a kinematic body back in mid-air.

```csharp
public static void SettleWhenReleased(Rigidbody body, bool kinematic, bool gravity)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | [`Rigidbody`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody.html) | The held object. |
| `kinematic` | [`bool`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean) | What it should be when the last hand lets go. |
| `gravity` | [`bool`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean) | Whether it should fall when the last hand lets go. |
